name: Fermi constant G_F = 1.1663788e-5 GeV^-2 and tree-level v = (sqrt(2) G_F)^(-1/2)

source.located: MEASUREMENT: MuLan, Tishchenko et al., Phys. Rev. D 87, 052003 (2013), arXiv:1211.0960 (final G_F); MuLan, Webber et al., PRL 106, 041803 (2011), arXiv:1010.0991 (the 1.1663788(7) value); PDG 2024 Table 1.1 'Physical Constants' (pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-phys-constants.pdf) lists G_F/(hbar c)^3 = 1.166 378 8(6)e-5 GeV^-2, the tree's exact pin. TREE RELATION: Buttazzo et al., JHEP 12 (2013) 089, arXiv:1307.3536, eqs. (8)-(11), Table 1-3 (V = (sqrt2 G_mu)^(-1/2) as the on-shell definition, with (1+Delta r)); MuLan 1211.0960 eqs. (2)-(3).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1211.0960 (pp.1-2, 28-30), 1010.0991 (pp.1,4), 1307.3536 (pp.4,6-8,13), the PDG 2024 physical-constants PDF by URL (p.1), CODATA 2022 arXiv:2409.03787 (pp.5,41,51). vRS 1999 (hep-ph/9808283) and Pak-Czarnecki 2008 are used only as restated in MuLan and Eberhart et al.; NAMED-NOT-READ themselves.

published_statement: MuLan 1211.0960 eq.(24): 'G_F(MuLan) = 1.166 378 7(6) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.5 ppm)', from eq.(23) G_F = sqrt(192 pi^3/(tau_mu m_mu^5)) (1+Dq0+Dq1+Dq2)^(-1/2) with tau_mu = 2 196 980.3(2.2) ps; the 2011 PRL (1010.0991 eq.5) printed 1.1663788(7). PDG 2024 Table 1.1: G_F/(hbar c)^3 = 1.166 378 8(6)e-5 GeV^-2. The relation to v: MuLan eq.(2) G_F/sqrt2 = g^2/(8 M_W^2)(1 + sum r_i); Buttazzo eq.(8)-(9): G_mu/sqrt2 = (1+Delta r_0)/(2 v_0^2), v_OS^2 = 1/(sqrt2 G_mu), delta v_OS^2 = -Delta r_0/(sqrt2 G_mu), i.e. v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) = 246.21971 GeV is the on-shell (G_mu-scheme) vev BY DEFINITION, the radiative corrections being moved into counterterms; the tree-level couplings built from it (lambda_OS = G_mu M_h^2/sqrt2 = 0.12917) differ from the MS-bar ones at mu = M_t (lambda = 0.12604 NNLO, m = 131.55 GeV).
published_hypotheses: V-A current-current Fermi interaction as the effective theory defining G_F: 'The above extraction of G_F from tau_mu is based on the assumption of the V - A chiral structure of the charged-current interaction. If the assumption of the V - A character is relinquished, the relation between tau_mu and G_F is modified' (1211.0960 p.29)
G_F universality: 'we assume that G_F is universal for weak interactions. Strictly speaking, tau_mu+ determines a muon-decay-specific coupling, denoted G_mu' (1010.0991 p.1)

QED corrections in Fermi theory to two loops (vRS) plus two-loop electron-mass terms (Pak-Czarnecki): Dq0 = -187.1, Dq1 = -4233.7, Dq2 = +36.3, and -0.4 ppm; theory uncertainty 0.14 ppm from unknown 3-loop QED (1211.0960 p.29)
free-muon lifetime equals the lifetime in the stopping targets (muonium vs mu+ difference ~0.6 ppb, Czarnecki-LePage-Marciano) (1211.0960 p.30)
convention: the tree-level W-propagator term 3 m_mu^2/(5 M_W^2) is absorbed into G_F (Buttazzo eq.27 removes it and gets G_mu = 1.1663781(6)e-5, '1 sigma lower')

tree relation: v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) holds exactly only as the on-shell definition of v; physically G_F/sqrt2 = (1+Delta r)/(2 v^2) (Buttazzo eq.8-9, MuLan eq.2-3); lambda = m_h^2/(2v^2) and V_min = -m_h^2 v^2/8 are tree-level (Buttazzo Table 1 'LO')

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. What the 2010-2013 MuLan authors lacked: (i) the O(alpha^3) QED correction and a modern dispersive hadronic term (they carried 0.14 ppm theory uncertainty from 'unknown 3-loop'); (ii) the CODATA 2018/2022 muon mass (105.6583755 vs 105.6583715 MeV) and exact hbar; (iii) later lifetime data entering the average (2196981.1 vs 2196980.3 ps). All three have since arrived: Eberhart et al. 2026 computed (i) and used (ii)-(iii), obtaining 1.16637859(59)e-5 -- 0.18 ppm (0.36 sigma) below the tree's pin, a move of 9.0e-8 in v and 1.8e-7 in rho_EW (COMPUTED). Evidence AGAINST the hypothesis for this result: having the data did not change the conclusion. Where data is still lacking: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision -- the EW-fit and CKM routes are ~1000x less precise and disagree with G_mu by +2 and -3 sigma (2102.02825), so whether G_mu carries a BSM admixture of order 1e-3 is OPEN; even the full 1e-3 would move v by <= 3.8e-4 and cannot move any order-of-magnitude figure. For the TREE RELATION the missing element is not data but a hypothesis: the tree uses LO lambda and V_min; the loop-level parameters were available (Buttazzo 2013, before the tree was written) and move lambda by -2.4 % and m^2 by +10.5 %.
grade_evidence: The MEASUREMENT half STANDS without qualification: the tree's pin 1.1663788e-5 is READ identically in PDG 2024 Table 1.1; every later READ value (MuLan 2013 1.1663787(6), CODATA 2022 1.1663787(6), Eberhart 2026 1.16637859(59)) lies within 0.18 ppm; the MuLan and 2026 extractions were re-run here (2026 reproduced to 2.5e-9; MuLan within 0.27 ppm of its print, a recorded discrepancy inside its 0.5 ppm error); no datum move exceeds 3e-7 in v. The TREE-RELATION half is narrowed by a hypothesis the owner drops: v = (sqrt2 G_F)^(-1/2) is exact only as the on-shell tree-level definition (Buttazzo eq.8-9; MuLan eq.2-3), and higgs.py:262-275 builds lambda and V_min at LO without naming 'tree level' anywhere in the owner (grep); the canonical entry names it, the owner does not. The size of the dropped hypothesis is COMPUTED from READ numbers: MS-bar NNLO lambda(M_t)/LO = 0.9757, m^2/M_h^2 = 1.105. Not WRONG: nothing is refuted, no counterexample exists, the tree-level formulae are correct at tree level (sympy A1-A3), and no order-of-magnitude figure (rho_EW ~ 2.5e45 J/m^3, xi_required ~ 1e32) moves. The grade is not raised to STANDS because the 1e-6 fixture digits on rho_EW and lambda are LO digits presented without the LO qualifier.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner names the tree-level (on-shell, LO) hypothesis at higgs.py:262-275 / excite.py:390 and the G_F status is updated to READ (PDG 2024 Table 1.1) -- then statement and hypotheses match the source. To DATA-DEPENDENT: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision that disagrees with G_mu (confirming a BSM admixture), and a tree conclusion that depends on v at the 1e-3 level (none found). To WRONG: only a computed contradiction of the tree relation at tree level, which sympy A1 excludes. Resolving the 0.27 ppm MuLan re-run discrepancy or the PDG-2024 (...788) vs CODATA-2022 (...787) last digit would not change the grade.
